newsitem.title: TAIWAN: New Taiwan soy-crushing plant breaks ground.
newsitem.headline: New Taiwan soy-crushing plant breaks ground.

text.p: Taiwan's Central Union Ltd broke ground on Tuesday for its planned T$1 billion (U$36 million) soybean crushing plant in the central port city of Taichung, executives said.
The crushing plant, expected to be completed in early 1998, will be able to crush 2,500 to 3,000 tonnes a day, a Central Union executive said.
Central Union is a joint venture formed by key members of Taiwan's main soybean buying interest, the Taichung division of the Breakfast Soybean Procurement Association.
Taiwan oilseed traders said the crushing plant would not significantly increase the island's soybean import volumes as association members planned to phase out old plants.
"The new crushing unit will replace their oil plants and keep the overall production at similar levels," a trader said.
Association members Chia Hsin Crop, Formosa Oilseeds Processing Co, Fwu Sow Grain Co and Tay Shan Enterprise have interests in the joint venture, the executive said.
Taiwan imported about 2.4 million tonnes of soybeans in 1996, mainly from the United States, traders said.
